outcome: maternal complications (chronic hypertension, pregnancy induced hypertension, pregestational diabetes mellitus, gestational diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism)
perinatal complications (cesarean section, small for gestational age, large for gestational age, stillbirths)
cohort: The study included women with singleton pregnancies, with a study group having BMI >= 50 kg/m^2 and a control group including all other women, who birthed at a single tertiary perinatal care center.
finding: Adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes, including chronic hypertension, gestational diabetes, and fetal growth abnormalities, are directly proportional to maternal obesity, with super obese women experiencing high rates of complications.
mod_finding: Super obese women experienced high rates of cesarean section (54%).
